description: Kanhe protocol objects of specification revision v0.10 (versions), built by an independent Python encoder from spec/kanhe.cddl. A school's ledger registers a clerk, delegated record statements on both of its form types (example.org.form/1 and /2), and a typist, delegated registrations of the second type only. Five versions of a form form one chain (`versions`, oldest first): each registration names the record it supersedes (key 6), across the two types; version 1 is endorsed and revoked after it was superseded; version 3 is revoked, and the organization's version 4 supersedes it all the same. The superseding registration is in both records' histories, so the state leaves list it twice. `refused` statements either break the CDDL (`malformed`: an id of 16 bytes in key 6) or are validated against the state after the first `after` statements, at `at`, and break exactly one rule, which `why` names: "superseded" (the record has a newer version already), "scope" (the signer's delegation does not cover the superseded record's type), "no such record", "mechanism" (a mechanism type, here a contract consent, on either side). `records` gives each record's type, state, revocation, registrant, history, endorsements, and the records it supersedes and that superseded it. `log_entries` holds the whole log, ending with the state commitment over `state_leaves`; `checkpoint` (signed at `checkpoint_time`) covers it. Signatures are Ed25519 (deterministic); keys are throwaway: seed = SHA-256("Kanhe test key: <name>").

statements.name: delegate both forms to the clerk
delegate only the second form to the typist
version 3, of the second type, supersedes version 2
endorse version 1 after it was superseded
the organization's version 4 supersedes the revoked version 3
revoke version 1 after it was superseded

refused.name: the typist supersedes version 2, of a type outside its scope
supersede version 1, revoked and superseded, again
supersede a record that does not exist
supersede with an id of 16 bytes
